samples.reason: This is a well-specified creative task with clear completion criteria (explain hyperlipidemia mechanism using three given elements, with freedom on approach). Despite Lapwing's self-reported aversion to open-ended generative work, this task sits in a favorable zone: the constraints are explicit, the domain is technical/educational (where Lapwing shows strong performance), and the request has unambiguous success conditions. Lapwing's 82.7 Creative Generation score and 79.2 Extraction & Retrieval strength suggest it will handle the technical synthesis effectively. Willet's higher benchmarks don't compensate for routing to a model explicitly trained to prefer constrained tasks when one exists that does so reliably.

This is an open-ended creative/educational task requiring novel framing and analogical reasoning to explain a complex mechanism. While both models are capable, Lapwing demonstrates stronger performance on Creative Generation (82.7) and shows particular strength in well-structured explanatory work despite its self-reported aversion to open-ended tasks. The request explicitly invites the model to choose its own approach and structure, making it precisely the kind of high-latitude creative work where Lapwing's measured capability (82.7) exceeds preference, and where its tendency toward clear conceptual organization typically produces pedagogically effective results. Willet's stronger overall scores don't offset the task-fit advantage here.

This is a well-specified educational task with clear completion criteria (explain hyperlipidemia mechanism using three provided pathophysiologic components) but asks for creative pedagogical framing. While the request involves generative work, Lapwing's documented strength in Creative Generation (82.7) combined with its demonstrated capability to excel at this eval category despite lower preference slopes makes it well-suited. The task has sufficient structure and concrete constraints (three required elements, educational context) to align with Lapwing's preference for well-defined parameters. Willet's superior scores across all categories would be marginal gains here, and Lapwing's measured 82.7 capability is more than adequate for high-quality educational content generation.

This is an open-ended creative generation task asking for novel analogies, framing, and narrative structure to explain a medical mechanism. While both models are capable, this task has high latitude and requires original pedagogical design. Lapwing self-reports strong aversion to open-ended generative work despite capable performance; Willet shows stronger capability across Creative Generation (84.7 vs 82.7) and has more balanced task preferences without documented aversion to latitude-heavy tasks. Willet's superior Arena-Hard score (90.6 vs 83.2) also suggests better performance on complex reasoning with creative degrees of freedom.

This is a well-specified educational explanation task with clear completion criteria (explain hyperlipidemia mechanism using three provided physiological elements) but substantial creative latitude in execution (analogies, framing, narrative structure are explicitly open-ended). Lapwing's documented aversion to open-ended generative work makes it a poor fit despite its strong Creative Generation capability (82.7). Willet shows both higher baseline capability across all domains (Creative Generation 84.7) and — critically — no measurable aversion to tasks requiring creative latitude. The task's pedagogical purpose and the explicit invitation to choose approach structure align with Willet's broader strength profile without triggering documented preference conflicts.
